## The problem

First-year cadets need intuition for model families, parameters, fit metrics and classification.

## Approach

sklearn scaled logistic regression with confusion matrix and odds ratios, where students score their own 'SIM' soldiers; seeded exponential/power/sinusoidal data where students tune sliders until NRMSE < 0.1.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Why it matters for a decision

Military-relevant classification framing (selection outcomes) and quantitative model-fit judgment.
:::

## Results

| Result | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Ruck-time odds ratio per minute (-10%) | Correct conversion coef/SD in notebook |

Every result above is traced to a script, log, or artifact in the repository. See [How I Check My Work](/approach.qmd).

## Limitations

- Ranger School data is synthetic
- MSE reported as classifier metric; |coef| 'importance' with collinear raw/points pairs
- Notebook needs a_hr/c_hr/d_hr_sims.csv, which are not in the repo; outputs include student-entered names
- param_find help text contradicts its model form (phase shift direction); answer password hardcoded; no README

## Tools

Python, scikit-learn, pandas, Streamlit, numpy, matplotlib
